headline: EFC (I) Limited to Acquire 100 percent Stake in Ultrafresh Modular Solutions Limited
sum: EFC (I) Limited announced acquisition of 100% stake in Ultrafresh Modular Solutions Limited. The transaction was disclosed via NSE press release intimation on 13 August 2026.
implication: 100% stake acquisition by a listed industrial company signals consolidation strategy in modular solutions; lawyers must verify CCI exemption thresholds, SEBI Listing Obligations compliance on related-party (if any) and material acquisition disclosure, and any anti-competitive trigger under the Competition Act.
detail: EFC (I) Limited, a listed entity on NSE, announced the acquisition of full ownership in Ultrafresh Modular Solutions Limited. The announcement was made via formal press release intimated to the NSE on 13 August 2026. Consideration amount, closing conditions, and timeline were not disclosed in the press release intimation itself. Further details on deal structure, regulatory approvals required (CCI, NCLT if applicable), and completion milestones would typically follow in subsequent stock exchange filings or supplementary disclosures.

framework.ref: SEBI Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements (LODR) 2015, Regulation 30
framework.note: Central — material events and acquisition announcements must be promptly disclosed to exchanges; 100% stake acquisition likely qualifies as material.
Central — if Ultrafresh is related to EFC or its promoters, RPT rules and board/shareholder approval protocols apply.
Central — acquisition of 100% stake is a 'combination' requiring CCI notification if turnover or asset thresholds are crossed; exemptions may apply for intra-group mergers.

framework.ref: Companies Act 2013, Section 230-232 (Merger/Amalgamation) & Section 5 (Definition of Company)
framework.note: Central — depending on structure (merger, asset purchase, or share purchase), Companies Act compliance (NCLT approval if merger, board & shareholder resolutions, etc.) is mandatory.
If Ultrafresh or EFC have non-resident shareholding or cross-border funding, FEMA notification/RBI approval may be required.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code 2016, Section 230A (Cross-border Insolvency)
framework.note: If either party is under insolvency proceedings or has defaulted debt, IBC implications must be vetted.
If acquisition structure requires merger sanction under CA s.230, NCLT approval and hearing procedures apply.

framework.ref: Income Tax Act 1961, Section 56 (Capital Gains) & Section 47-49 (Exemptions)
framework.note: Tax treatment of consideration, asset step-up, and relief under slump sale or merger provisions; advance notice to taxing authority advisable.
